# Roleplay Rule 8 - The Metashield
The "metashield" protects antagonist information from being widely known by characters who don't need to know it. This is so antagonists can have the chance to build up and so roleplay can naturally occur around finding out about them. Although [textlink="persistent character information" link="RuleMetagameOverview"] may bypass some of these protections, you’re expected to use your character’s knowledge for good roleplay, not to take down antagonists before they can create an interesting story.
[bold]Any antagonist that is not listed in your respective training manual is to be interpreted as something you do NOT know.[/bold] But in general, antagonist capabilities and tools are not known by the crew. Refer to the appropriate training manual below to know what is typically known by your role.
If you yourself are an antagonist, you will obviously know that you (and others like you) exist. Otherwise, you only have access to the appropriate training manual for your role. - If you’re a non-crew humanoid antagonist that doesn’t have a role on-station, such as a [textlink="Nuclear Operative" link="NuclearOperatives"] or a [textlink="Wizard" link="Wizard"], you know the about information in the [textlink="Crew Training Manual" link="CrewTrainingManual"] and the [textlink="Classified Training Manual." link="ClassifiedTrainingManual"] - Non-humanoid antagonists (such as the [textlink="Rat King" link="MinorAntagonists"], [textlink="Space Dragons" link="MinorAntagonists"], and [textlink="Xenoborgs" link="Xenoborgs"]) do not get access to the manuals’ knowledge.
If you are a [textlink="Traitor" link="Traitors"] or other Syndicate member, you will also know about the [textlink="Gorlex Marauders" link="NuclearOperatives"] and their type of work. You should only help them if you have the objective "die a glorious death."
## Explicitly Shielded
The following is a list of explicitly shielded things, which means that regardless of manual, your character definitely shouldn’t know about these: - Chameleon items, such as no-slip shoes, that are [italic]locked[/italic] cannot be suspected of being chameleon. They must be real good on their feet or something... (If you can change the item’s appearance through the Chameleon menu, or if an EMP causes the item to change, then you’re aware of the item’s chameleon properties. [italic]You should not randomly EMP people to check if their clothing is chameleon! Admin help (F1) if this happens![/italic]) - Non-Nanotrasen implants cannot be suspected unless there is absolutely, physically no other possible way that something could’ve happened. (A SCRAM implant could’ve been a bluespace crystal, or a storage implant might actually be a clever stash in a plant pot...) If there is [italic]any[/italic] doubt, then you should not be attempting to remove an implant. Your character [italic]is[/italic] allowed to suspect implants if they find the used implanter itself, though.
## Precedents
- Your character should use common sense on when to report things, even if they don’t know the specifics. If someone’s murdered, report it. If someone robs you, report it. If you have a valuable, one-of-a-kind item, you should keep an eye on it. Report what people [italic]do[/italic], not what people [italic]are[/italic]. - Your character can know another character's typical appearance, but keep in mind that multiple people can share the same name. - Unless mentioned in your role’s manual, you should avoid calling out the name of the antagonist if you can help it. Calling out “Terrorists at the bridge!" instead of “[bold]NUKIES BRIDGE!!![/bold]" helps to make a more immersive story.
## Training Manuals
All crew have access to the Crew Training Manual (and in-character can access [italic]this manual[/italic] through their PDAs — you can find these manuals out-of-character [textlink="in the guidebook" link="TrainingManuals"]). Some jobs have additional information provided in their respective sections (information which other civilian jobs do not know about). - [textlink="Crew Training Manual" link="CrewTrainingManual"]
[bold]If your role has access to any of the manuals below, your character is expected to treat the given knowledge as classified![/bold] [italic]There are in-character and out-of-character consequences for having classified knowledge becoming public too early or for no good reason![/italic] (Unless you’re an antagonist, that is...)
Some crew jobs get special, extended access to their training manuals. - [color=#42636d][bold]Medical[/bold][/color] staff have this extra knowledge: [textlink="MEDICAL ONLY" link="CrewTrainingManualAllMedical"] - [color=#388c34][bold]Chaplains[/bold][/color] get their own addendum, too: [textlink="CHAPLAIN ONLY" link="CrewTrainingManualChaplain"] - [color=#388c34][bold]Librarians[/bold][/color] may access [bold]both[/bold] the above addendums. They speak Eldritch; they should know a thing or two. (They also may know about the Wizard Federation — see "Optional Job Knowledge.")
Members of [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color], [color=#1b67a5][bold]Command[/bold][/color], and [color=#1e7f28][bold]Central Command[/bold][/color] have access to the Classified Training Manual and [bold]all[/bold] information in the Crew Training Manual, [italic]including the above job-specific sections[/italic]. [bold]Reading the manual from the in-game “Classified Training Manual" item gives you full access to [bolditalic]specifically this manual’s[/bolditalic] knowledge, too[/bold] (such as from the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Captain[/bold][/color]’s or [color=#1b67a5][bold]Head of Security[/bold][/color]’s lockers). - [textlink="Classified Training Manual" link="ClassifiedTrainingManual"]
Only [color=#1e7f28][bold]Central Command Officials/Dignitaries[/bold][/color] know the contents of the Dignitary Training Manual. - [textlink="Dignitary Training Manual" link="DignitaryTrainingManual"]
### Optional Job Knowledge
Though not included in the manuals, some information could be gained from prior employment experience. If you are one of these roles mentioned below, it’s up to you whether or not your character will know that information. (It may be more fun to not know.) - [color=#388c34][bold]Librarians[/bold][/color] may know about the Wizard Federation and what typical Wizards look like, if they're a nerd or superstitiously inclined. - [color=#cc74fc]Science[/color] personnel may know the basic features of [textlink="Xenomorphs" link="Xenomorphs"], such as the fact they reproduce through a parasitic facehugger, [bold]but they will not know specific castes[/bold]. - [color=#388c34][bold]Chefs[/bold][/color] may have seen a [textlink="large hyperintelligent rodent" link="MinorAntagonists"] attempt to establish itself via consuming large quantities of their food to raise a swarm of rats. - The [color=#1b67a5][bold]Head of Security[/bold][/color], the [color=#ba292c][bold]Warden[/bold][/color], or the [color=#ba292c][bold]Sergeant[/bold][/color] may know of the intricacies of [color=#ff0000]Syndicate[/color] weapory, such as their names and functions. (This specific knowledge should be reserved for true gun fanatics.)
